target_customer: Commercial office building owners and cleaning contractors
problem: Cleaning office bathrooms is unpleasant, labor intensive work with high turnover that existing floor robots cannot do.
business_model: Robot as a service lease, about 1,000 USD per month in trial per TechCrunch

founders.name: Michael Levy
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built Chalkable; TechCrunch says he started with bathroom jobs at his grandfather's restaurant.

founders.name: Eugene Zasoba
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder and CTO by TechCrunch and the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile manipulation robot that opens doors and cleans toilets, trained via remote VR, needs custom hardware, perception and teleoperation.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware plus teleoperation data are hard to copy, but the market is small and well funded floor cleaning robot firms could extend.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent moved into restroom robots in the sources opened.

market_need_then: March 2020 TechCrunch said the robot already cleaned offices of a FAANG customer and a handful of others, targeting about 8 hours of cleaning a day.

branding.domain_note: Uses getsomatic.com, a get prefix rather than the exact .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Blunt, product first: bathroom cleaning robots

branding.brand_signature: The bathroom cleaning robot, described as a minifridge with an arm
branding.community_and_virality: Viral style coverage from TechCrunch, PopSci, Fox News and Core77 about the robot, not the name.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable, easily explained product drew repeated press coverage, though the name itself was not discussed.

outcome_analysis: Somatic built a restroom cleaning robot trained by remote VR and sold it as a lease. It had early customers in 2020 and a reported 13.7M Series A in February 2025. It is still active, but heavy hardware costs and few funding details leave the outcome unproven.
notes: Funding conflicts: Bouncewatch lists 7.31M total, VCBacked 13.7M, Caplight 21.15M and a headline about a 16M Series A led by BlackRock and Fin Capital (unverified, likely a different company); the 13.7M figure matches an SEC filing per a search summary. Named investors differ by source and are not adopted. The TechCrunch 2020 amounts are 50K bootstrapped plus 300K including 150K from SOSV. Education not found. Competitors: 2020 TechCrunch names none; Brain Corp, Avidbots and Peanut Robotics came only from undated aggregator pages, so the list is empty. Company is described as New York based in press but YC lists Miami Beach.
